title: Commutativity preserving mappings in Banach algebras
summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be unital complex Banach algebras having no quotients isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}$ or $M_2(\mathbb{C})$. Assume additionally that $B$ is semisimple. If a surjective additive mapping $Φ\colon A\to B$ satisfies $[Φ(x^2),Φ(x)] = 0$ for all $x\in A$, then there exist a surjective direct sum of an additive homomorphism and an additive anti-homomorphism $Ψ\colon A\to B$, an invertible element $λ\in\mathcal{Z}(B)$, and an additive mapping $ζ\colon A\to\mathcal{Z}(B)$ such that $Φ(x)=λΨ(x)+ζ(x)$ for all $x\in A$.
